parties: Al Maha Investment Fund PCC – ONYX Strategy / Indigo Infracon Private Limited / Lake Shore Realty Limited
headline: Al Maha and Indigo Infracon acquire 54.84% of Lake Shore Realty; mandatory open offer receives 17 shares
sum: Al Maha (38.39%) and Indigo Infracon (16.45%) jointly purchased 19,19,630 Lake Shore Realty shares from six former promoters for ₹11.04 crore. A mandatory 26% open offer at ₹57.51 drew only 17 accepted shares, not the 9,10,182-share maximum.
detail: Transaction and status (2025): Under a share purchase agreement dated 30 May 2025, Category I foreign portfolio investor Al Maha Investment Fund PCC – ONYX Strategy (Acquirer 1) and Indigo Infracon Private Limited (Acquirer 2) acquired, in aggregate, 19,19,630 fully paid-up ₹10 shares representing 54.84% of the voting share capital of BSE-listed Lake Shore Realty Limited (formerly Mahaan Foods Limited; BSE 519612; CIN L68100DL1987PLC350285), from six selling promoter shareholders. The contractual price was ₹57.51 per share, totalling ₹11,03,97,921.30, payable in cash. The 70:30 distribution between the buyers was Al Maha 13,43,741 shares (38.39% of target voting capital) and Indigo Infracon 5,75,889 shares (16.45%). The six selling promoters were Aditya Goyal, Sanjeev Goyal, Saloni Goyal, Sanya Goyal, Sanjeev Goyal HUF and Priyanka Sethi; their seller-wise share breakdown is preserved in the structured deal record. The sellers ceased holding those sale shares and transferred management/control; the LOF states Indigo Infracon would be classified as promoter and the sellers reclassified in accordance with SEBI LODR Regulation 31A. The LOF states the underlying SPA transaction had been consummated under SAST Regulations 22(2) and 17; the acquisition is not a scheme of arrangement or indirect takeover. Mandatory open offer: The joint purchase and change of control triggered SEBI (SAST) Regulations 3(1) and 4. The buyers offered to purchase up to 9,10,182 further shares (26% of equity/voting capital) at the same ₹57.51 cash price, a maximum offer consideration of ₹5,23,44,566.82. The acquirers agreed to allocate offer shares 70:30 if fully subscribed (6,37,128 Al Maha / 2,73,054 Indigo Infracon). They deposited 100% of the maximum offer consideration in an Axis Bank escrow; this was not a minimum-acceptance or conditional offer. Open-offer tendering ran 13–28 October 2025. Crucially, the 10 November 2025 post-offer advertisement states only 17 public shares were tendered AND accepted, for just ₹977.67; the aggregate SPA-plus-offer holding immediately after the 2025 offer was thus 19,19,647 shares, still approximately 54.84%. The 80.83% figure sometimes shown in the Letter of Offer is a full-acceptance PROJECTION, not the actual holding. Deal mechanics and restrictive covenants: The SPA summary provides for condition precedents, unencumbered demat transfer against bank remittance, nominee directors, transfer of management/control, and reclassification/stock-exchange disclosures. The SPA includes a 10-year post-completion undertaking against the target engaging in dairy or dairy nutrition activities and restrictions on using the 'Mahaan'/'MFL' intellectual-property and brand names. It also required a change in registered office after closing. SEBI compliance includes open-offer pricing under Regulation 8, full escrow under Regulation 17, offer timetable and public-announcement obligations, plus minimum public shareholding under SEBI LODR Regulation 38/SCRR Rule 19A (relevant if an offer had been fully accepted). Almondz Financial Services Limited was Manager to the Offer, and Alankit Assignments Limited Registrar to the Offer; neither is identified here as transaction legal counsel. Dated, separate monitoring: Public disclosures in April 2026 report Al Maha-related share disposals and 2 November 2026 disclosures report further board/office decisions. Those later events must be assessed separately; the 2025 post-offer holdings are NOT represented as the current 2026 cap table.
implication: Listed-company takeover precedent: distinguish the 54.84% jointly acquired under the SPA from Indigo Infracon's individual 16.45% allocation; distinguish a 26% mandatory open-offer CAP from only 17 shares ACTUALLY accepted. Check the 70:30 inter-acquirer MOU, SAST Regulations 3(1), 4, 7, 8, 17, 18(12) and 22(2), full-cash escrow, seller reclassification, control changes, minimum public-shareholding sensitivity and 10-year dairy/branding restrictions. The disclosed 2025 closing does not establish November 2026 ownership after subsequent disposals.

parties: Marico Limited (buyer), Cosmix Wellness Private Limited (target)
headline: Marico completes additional 20% Cosmix purchase for ₹113.65 crore, increasing ownership to 80%
sum: Completed 6 November 2026: Marico acquired another 20% of Cosmix Wellness for ₹113.65 crore cash, lifting its stake from 60% to 80%. Its future right to buy the remaining 20% has not been exercised.
detail: Marico's signed exchange disclosure confirms a completed acquisition of an additional 20% stake in its Bengaluru-headquartered subsidiary Cosmix Wellness Private Limited on 6 November 2026 for ₹113.65 crore in cash. It already held 60% following a February 2026 purchase; the additional tranche brings ownership to 80%. The issuer describes the deal as an arm's-length related-party transaction, confirms no promoter interest and states that government/regulatory approvals were not required. The separate right to acquire the remaining 20% only after FY2028-29 is conditional on milestones, requisite approvals and negotiated terms and is not an executed sale. Cosmix reported ₹91.53 crore turnover in FY2025-26 compared with ₹47.25 crore in FY2024-25 and ₹24.32 crore for FY2023-24 (Indian GAAP).
implication: Staged subsidiary buyout: distinguish a completed second tranche from an unexercised later right; analyse RPT requirements and retained minority rights without inventing undisclosed contract protections.

parties: Bajaj Finance Limited (issuer); qualified institutional buyers (investors)
headline: Bajaj Finance completes ₹11,700-crore QIP allotment of 114.15 million shares at ₹1,025
sum: Allotment approved 17 November 2026: 114,146,341 equity shares allotted at ₹1,025 each, above the ₹992.25 floor, for approximately ₹11,700 crore. A separately announced ₹5,800-crore promoter-warrant issue is not included.
detail: Bajaj Finance's QIP Allotment Committee filing reports allotment of 114,146,341 fully paid-up ₹1 equity shares to QIBs at ₹1,025 per share (including ₹1,024 premium), above the ₹992.25 SEBI ICDR floor, totalling approximately ₹117,000 million (₹11,700 crore). Paid-up equity shares rose from 6,225,954,304 to 6,340,100,645. Annexure A lists ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund with 11,707,317 shares (10.26% of QIP issue size) and Government Pension Fund Global with 5,849,421 (5.12% of QIP issue size), not percentages of the company's total capital. The separately reported ₹5,800-crore issue of promoter warrants to Bajaj Finserv is a different transaction and not part of this QIP. The issuer filing proves allotment and economics; Bar & Bench independently names issuer-side and placement-agent-side counsel.
implication: QIP precedent: reconcile issue price and floor, capital before/after, allotment approval, and issue-level investor percentages. Never add separately issued promoter warrants to QIP proceeds.

parties: Aegis Logistics Limited (issuer); qualified institutional buyers
headline: Aegis Logistics closes ₹3,500-crore QIP; 28.93 million shares allocated at ₹1,210
sum: Issue closed 16 November 2026: Aegis' fund-raising committee approved allocation of 28,925,619 shares at ₹1,210 each and adopted the placement document. The disclosed closing/allocation should not be mislabelled as a separate final allotment confirmation.
detail: Aegis Logistics's NSE disclosure confirms that its institutional placement opened on 11 November 2026 and was closed on 16 November after receipt of applications and escrow funds from eligible QIBs. Its fundraising committee approved allocation of 28,925,619 shares of face value ₹1 at ₹1,210 per share, including ₹1,209 share premium, an implied aggregate of approximately ₹3,500 crore. The 16 November placement document and confirmation-of-allocation notice were also approved. This original document records closure and allocation; a separate final allotment filing should be checked before describing the actual legal allotment as already completed. Bar & Bench separately reports AZB & Partners and Hogan Lovells Cadwalader advising the issuer on Indian and international law, and Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas and Linklaters advising the placement agents on Indian and international law. The placement agents are investment banks, not law firms.
implication: Separate issue close, share allocation and actual allotment; reconcile 28,925,619 × ₹1,210, cite the precise issuer filing for mechanics, and credit the four law firms only to their reported legal mandates.
